title: Entanglement in the ring — 43 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Entanglement in the ring. 43 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/z9plus.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 32 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 11 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 12 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 164 pairs; the theorems fall into 7 strands, the largest of 23. Most binding: m9 (10), pw (10), R (7), fib (6), dr (5), closure (5).

2 · Imports. Built on: reversal.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/z9plus.lean, src/proof/reversal.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 43 sealed receipts fold to 49d7127a-322e-824e-980a-901b45ec0468. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (8, 5, 1, 3, 4, 7, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: coin.lean (10 observed, 4.98 expected, lift 2.01), fnv.lean (10 observed, 5.4 expected, lift 1.85), phenomena.lean (3 observed, 1.66 expected, lift 1.81). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.14 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 62.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.54; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.48. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 614abe8701b2 (2026-09-15), over 726 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Digital roots (casting out nines) — in use by the 12th century; the Pisano period — after Leonardo Pisano; studied by Joseph-Louis Lagrange, 1774. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. squares_land_exactly_in_zero_one_four_seven — R.all (fun d => [0, 1, 4, 7].contains (m9 (d * d))) ∧ [0, 1, 4, 7].all (fun s => R.any (fun d => m9 (d * d) == s)) record
  2. five_is_not_a_square_mod_nine — ¬ (R.any (fun d => m9 (d * d) == 5)) record
  3. cubes_land_exactly_in_zero_one_eight — R.all (fun d => [0, 1, 8].contains (pw d 3)) ∧ [0, 1, 8].all (fun c => R.any (fun d => pw d 3 == c)) record
  4. primitive_roots_are_exactly_two_and_five — (R.filter generates) = [2, 5] record
  5. primitive_root_iff_generates_the_units — R.all (fun g => generates g == ([2, 5].contains g)) record
  6. doubling_has_period_six — (List.range 30).all (fun k => pw 2 k == pw 2 (k + 6)) record
  7. no_period_smaller_than_six — ¬ ([1, 2, 3, 4, 5].any (fun p => (List.range 12).all (fun k => pw 2 k == pw 2 (k + p)))) record
  8. digital_root_agrees_with_the_residue — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => (dr n == 9) == (m9 n == 0)) record
  9. digital_root_is_the_digit_sum_residue — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => m9 (digitSum n) == m9 n) record
  10. reversal_cannot_change_the_digital_root — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => dr (reverseNum n) == dr n) record
  11. orbit_digital_roots_have_period_six — (List.range 24).all (fun k => dr (pw 2 k) == dr (pw 2 (k + 6))) record
  12. the_orders_of_the_units_are_exact — ord 1 = 1 ∧ ord 8 = 2 ∧ ord 4 = 3 ∧ ord 7 = 3 ∧ ord 2 = 6 ∧ ord 5 = 6 record
  13. the_unit_table_is_a_latin_square — [1,2,4,5,7,8].all (fun a => (([1,2,4,5,7,8].map (fun b => m9 (a * b))).eraseDups).length == 6 ∧ [1,2,4,5,7,8].all (fun c => [1,2,4,5,7,8].any (fun b => m9 (a * b) == c))) record
  14. the_orbit_never_meets_the_triad — (List.range 40).all (fun k => ! [0, 3, 6].contains (pw 2 k)) record
  15. the_reflected_orbit_covers_the_whole_triad — [3, 6, 9].all (fun t => orbit6.any (fun d => refl d == t)) record
  16. reflection_splits_the_orbit_in_half — (orbit6.filter (fun d => [3, 6, 9].contains (refl d))).length = 3 ∧ (orbit6.filter (fun d => ! [3, 6, 9].contains (refl d))).length = 3 record
  17. the_crossing_pairs_are_one_four_seven — (orbit6.filter (fun d => [3, 6, 9].contains (refl d))) = [1, 4, 7] ∧ refl 1 = 9 ∧ refl 4 = 6 ∧ refl 7 = 3 record
  18. reflection_is_injective_on_the_orbit — ((orbit6.map refl).eraseDups).length = 6 record
  19. doubling_alone_reaches_only_the_units — ((List.range 12).map (fun k => pw 2 k)).eraseDups.length = 6 ∧ ((List.range 12).map (fun k => pw 2 k)).all (fun d => ! [0, 3, 6].contains d) record
  20. reflection_alone_reaches_only_two — (closure 6 [1]).length ≥ 2 ∧ rfl9 1 = 0 ∧ rfl9 (rfl9 1) = 1 record
  21. doubling_and_reflection_together_reach_every_residue — (closure 4 [1]).length = 9 record
  22. every_residue_is_reachable_from_one — (List.range 9).all (fun d => (closure 4 [1]).contains d) record
  23. the_diameter_is_exactly_four — (closure 4 [1]).length = 9 ∧ (closure 3 [1]).length = 7 record
  24. the_frontier_grows_by_two_each_round — (closure 0 [1]).length = 1 ∧ (closure 1 [1]).length = 3 ∧ (closure 2 [1]).length = 5 ∧ (closure 3 [1]).length = 7 ∧ (closure 4 [1]).length = 9 record
  25. product_of_the_units_is_minus_one — m9 ([1,2,4,5,7,8].foldl (· * ·) 1) = 8 ∧ m9 (8 + 1) = 0 record
  26. pisano_period_mod_nine_is_twenty_four — (List.range 30).all (fun k => fib9 k == fib9 (k + 24)) record
  27. no_proper_divisor_of_twenty_four_is_a_period — ¬ ([1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12].any (fun p => (List.range 26).all (fun k => fib9 k == fib9 (k + p)))) record
  28. fibonacci_recurrence_holds — (List.range 20).all (fun n => fib (n + 2) == fib n + fib (n + 1)) record
  29. consecutive_fibonacci_are_coprime — (List.range' 1 25).all (fun n => gcd9 (fib n) (fib (n + 1)) == 1) record
  30. three_five_eight_are_consecutive_fibonacci — fib 4 = 3 ∧ fib 5 = 5 ∧ fib 6 = 8 ∧ fib 4 + fib 5 = fib 6 record
  31. units_and_triad_partition_the_ring — ((R.filter (fun d => R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).length + (R.filter (fun d => ! R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).length) = 9 record
  32. both_parts_sum_to_zero — m9 ((R.filter (fun d => R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).foldl (· + ·) 0) == 0 ∧ m9 ((R.filter (fun d => ! R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).foldl (· + ·) 0) == 0 record
  33. doubling_has_period_six_for_every_k — ∀ k : Nat, pw 2 (k + 6) = pw 2 k record
  34. orbit_digital_roots_have_period_six_for_every_k — ∀ k : Nat, dr (pw 2 (k + 6)) = dr (pw 2 k) record
  35. the_doubling_orbit_is_read_from_the_exponent_mod_six — ∀ k : Nat, pw 2 k = pw 2 (k % 6) record
  36. the_orbit_never_meets_the_triad_for_every_k — ∀ k : Nat, pw 2 k ≠ 0 ∧ pw 2 k ≠ 3 ∧ pw 2 k ≠ 6 record
  37. fibonacci_residues_mod_nine_repeat_every_twenty_four_steps — ∀ k : Nat, fib (k + 24) % 9 = fib k % 9 ∧ fib (k + 25) % 9 = fib (k + 1) % 9 record
  38. pisano_period_mod_nine_is_twenty_four_for_every_k — ∀ k : Nat, fib9 (k + 24) = fib9 k record
  39. the_fuelled_gcd_is_the_gcd_when_the_fuel_exceeds_the_second_argument — ∀ f a b : Nat, b < f → gcdF f a b = Nat.gcd a b record
  40. consecutive_fibonacci_numbers_are_coprime — ∀ n : Nat, Nat.gcd (fib n) (fib (n + 1)) = 1 record
  41. consecutive_fibonacci_are_coprime_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, gcd9 (fib n) (fib (n + 1)) = 1 record
  42. digital_root_agrees_with_the_residue_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 0 < n → (dr n = 9 ↔ m9 n = 0) record
  43. digital_root_is_the_digit_sum_residue_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, m9 (digitSum n) = m9 n record
